name: Tapestry, Inc.
key_signal: TPR trades at a rich trailing P/E (43x) but a much cheaper forward P/E (18x) on the back of 73.7% earnings growth and 21.2% revenue growth, even as the stock has pulled back ~13% from its 52-week high and sits right at its 50-day moving average.
thesis: Tapestry's fundamentals are unusually strong for a mid-cap luxury name: 76% gross margins, 22% operating margins, ROE north of 60%, and forward P/E of 18x versus a trailing 43x implies the market is pricing in a sharp earnings inflection that is already showing up in the 73.7% earnings growth figure. The stock remains above both its 50- and 200-day moving averages with an active golden cross, and the 126-day momentum is still positive (+6.6%), suggesting the medium-term uptrend from the Capri-deal collapse recovery is intact despite a recent 3-month pullback (-9.3%) that has reset RSI to a neutral 47.6 — a healthier entry point than a name still overbought near highs. bear_case: The near-term technicals are actually deteriorating — mom_21d and mom_63d are both negative, MACD histogram is solidly negative (-0.366), and price is essentially flat against its 50dma (141.02 vs 140.83), meaning the stock has stalled right at a key support/resistance level after rolling over from 161.97; a break below the 50dma with negative MACD momentum could quickly test the 200dma near 133. Fundamentally, the balance sheet carries an alarming debt-to-equity of 575%, a legacy of aggressive buybacks that have hollowed out book value (priceToBook of 41.8x is not a quality signal, it's a leverage signal), leaving little cushion if the high-margin growth story stumbles amid a high-beta (1.44), high-volatility (33.6% annualized) profile in a discretionary category vulnerable to consumer pullback; if forward earnings growth disappoints even modestly, the stock re-rates on trailing multiples rather than forward ones, and 43x trailing PE offers no margin of safety.
